investigacion.base:
As of October 19, 2026, Amazon hasn't reported Q3 results yet, so the question can't resolve today. The best anchors are Amazon's guidance of **$197–202B**, with a midpoint of 199.5, and analyst consensus of about **$202B**. Amazon has usually landed at or above the top of its guidance range.

**Resolution sources**
- **Amazon IR quarterly results page:** I couldn't load it directly. The latest release on it is the Q2 2026 release from July 30, 2026, and no Q3 release exists yet. The Q3 call is set for October 29 at 2:00 p.m. PT/5:00 p.m. ET. TipRanks lists the date as After Close (Confirmed).
- **Metaculus FAQ "credible sources":** This is a general definition (major news outlets, official filings). It doesn't affect resolution here beyond letting the 8-K or press coverage confirm the number.

**Guidance (Q2 release, July 30, 2026)**
- Net sales are expected to be between $197.0 billion and $202.0 billion, or to grow between 9% and 12% compared with third quarter 2025. Q3 2025 net sales were $180.17B.
- Excluding the impact of Prime Day in both 2025 and 2026, third quarter 2026 year-over-year growth would be nearly 400 basis points higher. This guidance anticipates an unfavorable impact of approximately 80 basis points from foreign exchange rates. Most of Prime Day moved into Q2 this year, while in 2025, Prime Day was entirely in Q3.
- Operating income guidance is between $22.5 billion and $26.5 billion, compared with $17.4 billion in third quarter 2025.

**Recent results and momentum**
- Q2 2026: net sales increased 20% to $200.6 billion. AWS grew 37%, its fastest rate in 18 quarters.
- Q2 2026 guidance had been $194–199B (to grow between 16% and 19%). The actual $200.6B beat the top of that range by about $1.6B.
- Analysts expect AWS revenue to grow 30%-35% year over year in the third quarter (Motley Fool, Oct 16).

**Consensus**
- Benzinga, Oct 19: Analysts estimate earnings per share of $1.96 and revenue of $202.21 billion.
- MarketBeat: expected revenue of $202.03 billion. An older MarketBeat figure from right after Q2 was $204.6B.
- Before guidance came out, the estimate was $203.93B. Analysts trimmed their numbers toward the top of the guidance range afterward.

**Base rate: actual results vs. guidance.** These come from my memory of Amazon's releases except the Q2 2026 and Q3 2025 figures, so please verify them:

| Quarter | Guidance | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 2025 | $151–155.5B | $155.7B |
| Q2 2025 | $159–164B | $167.7B |
| Q3 2025 | $174–179.5B | $180.2B |
| Q4 2025 | $206–213B | about $213.4B |
| Q2 2026 | $194–199B | $200.6B |

Amazon typically comes in at the top of its range or $0.5–4B above it. Applied to this quarter, that points to roughly $202–205B. It also beat revenue consensus in Q3 2024 ($158.88B vs. $157.28B) and Q3 2025 ($180.17B vs. $177.53B).

**Scheduled events before resolution**
- Alphabet and Microsoft report around Oct 27, which gives a read on cloud demand.
- Amazon reports Q3 after market close on Oct 29.

**Other notes**
- FX: 80 basis points of the guidance's headwind assumption comes from exchange rates as of July. Any dollar moves since then could shift the result by about ±$1B.
- I found no prediction-market prices for this question.

criterios: This question resolves based on the total "Net sales" figure Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) reports for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026, in its official quarterly earnings release, expected after market close on October 29, 2026. The value is the consolidated total net sales for the quarter, in US dollars (e.g., reported net sales of $205.3 billion resolves as 205.3). The earnings release will be available on Amazon's investor relations quarterly results page (https://ir.aboutamazon.com/quarterly-results/default.aspx); the figure may also be confirmed via Amazon's 8-K filing or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). If Amazon has not released its Q3 2026 results by the resolution date due to a scheduling change, the question is annulled.
letra_pequena: Only the headline consolidated "Net sales" figure for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 counts, not segment-level sales, trailing-twelve-month figures, or any "excluding foreign exchange" adjusted value. If the release restates the figure after initial publication, the value as first reported in the earnings release governs.

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days until Amazon’s scheduled October 29 release. The quarter ended September 30, so its sales are already determined, though not yet reported.

(b) **If nothing changed:** Amazon’s guidance points to $197–202 billion, with a $199.5 billion midpoint.

(c) **If the recent trend continued:** Results near or modestly above the top of guidance would imply roughly $202–205 billion.

(d) **Experts and markets:** Analyst estimates cluster near $202 billion. Recent revenue beats support a forecast slightly above that figure, but are not a guarantee.

(e) **Unexpected low outcome:** Weaker-than-anticipated sales or an unfavorable foreign-exchange effect could put reported sales below guidance.

(f) **Unexpected high outcome:** Stronger AWS growth or favorable foreign-exchange movements could produce a larger-than-usual beat.

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. Amazon reports after market close on October 29, 2026.

(b) **If nothing changed:** Taking guidance at face value gives a midpoint of $199.5B. Amazon rarely lands near its midpoint, though, so this is a conservative floor-type anchor rather than a likely outcome.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** Amazon has come in at or above the top of its guidance range in every quarter listed. The amounts above the top were +$0.2B, +$3.7B, +$0.7B, +$0.4B and +$1.6B. Applying that to the $202B top gives roughly $202.5–205B, centered near $203B. Momentum supports this:
- AWS grew 37% last quarter.
- Underlying growth, excluding the Prime Day shift into Q2, is about 13–16%.

(d) **Experts and markets:** Consensus is about $202.0–202.2B (Benzinga, MarketBeat). Some older or aggregator figures run up to about $204B. Amazon has beaten revenue consensus by roughly 1–2.4% in recent quarters, which would imply about $204–206B. That full beat rate looks less likely here because analysts have already moved to the top of the range.

(e) **Low scenario:** The dollar strengthens sharply after July, adding to the FX headwind. Retail demand also softens more than expected after the Prime Day pull-forward into Q2. Net sales land around $198–200B, inside the guidance range.

(f) **High scenario:** AWS accelerates further on AI demand toward 38–40%, the dollar weakens (an FX tailwind), and advertising and retail are strong. That produces about $206–208B, similar to the $3.7B beat over the top of guidance in Q2 2025.

(c) **If the recent trend continued:** Another modest beat of the guidance ceiling would put sales around $203–204 billion.  
(d) **Experts and markets:** Analyst consensus is near $202 billion.  
(e) **Unexpected low outcome:** Weaker AWS growth or an adverse currency move could bring sales below guidance, toward $195–197 billion.  
(f) **Unexpected high outcome:** Stronger AWS and retail sales could push the result above $206 billion. October’s Prime Big Deal Days falls in Q4, so it would not directly add to Q3 sales.
